key_points: At domainspec-core commit 7e77af60ea1fa80fca20d3ebe1df41e2391df149, the tracked dialectic review classifies WAY-MAKER.md as FIX and states that its Stage 1 acceptance requirements do not yet close admission, typed identity, duplicate reduction, or independent-fixture obligations.

The reviewed repair shape separates raw admission, semantic normalization, canonical payload bytes, typed semantic digest, event/cursor reduction, and fixture identity; the review leaves the governing choices with the RWO planning/design owner.

The canonical WAY-MAKER.md source path is not present in reachable objects or fetched refs of the configured domainspec-core remote, including origin/master and origin/factory-ai-vladimir-handoff; only the tracked review references are available here.

At domainspec-lean-formalization commit 7b18feff9b0ea6bc5c977c021d3cab78a1aa82a1, existing Lean artifacts provide model-level patterns for admission boundaries, idempotent normalization, exact structural closure, duplicate/replay counterexamples, and authority/lifecycle separation, but none is a correspondence proof for the Waymaker runtime.

AgentLanguageIndependence.kernel_admits_rootless_delegation shows that the current K1-K6 model admits a rootless delegation cycle; anti-self-blessing is therefore an open proof obligation rather than an established guarantee.
